acceptance_criteria: AC-1 An authenticated GET of the session status returns the session's CSRF token under the key the client reads.
AC-2 The returned token equals the secret stored on that session row, and a different session gets a different token.
AC-3 An unauthenticated caller's response is byte-for-byte what it is today and contains no token key.
AC-4 A state-changing request carrying that token is admitted; one without it is still refused with 401 SESSION_INVALID, unchanged.
AC-5 The response cannot be cached: a test asserts the no-store headers.
AC-6 The token appears in no log line at any level; a test or an inspection named in the SESSION_CLOSE establishes it.
AC-7 The ui2 service tests and the frontend suite pass with the new tests, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_C3_IDENTITY_SESSIONS_RBAC_CONTRACT.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner approved 2026-09-09. Its sessions schema declares `csrf_secret TEXT NOT NULL -- opaque, minted at session creation, never logged`. Its identity section states the secret is minted at session creation, never logged, and required on every state-changing request. Its gate table makes E1 refuse a state-changing method whose CSRF token is absent or does not match `sessions.csrf_secret`, with 401 SESSION_INVALID. The contract requires the client to present the token; it does not say the client may never be told it, and no clause forbids returning it on the authenticated session-status response. This movement closes that gap and changes no gate, no schema and no status code.
baseline.engineering_baseline: GateChain checks the token only for state-changing methods, after the session row is found and before the origin check. The frontend requests the token before each write and omits the header when it cannot get one.
baseline.product_baseline: An operator can sign in and read every screen. Every write is refused with SESSION_INVALID. Reported by the Product Owner on 2026-09-15 while creating an identity; the same refusal explains a credential that appeared not to save.
baseline.test_baseline: The ui2 service and frontend suites pass on origin/main today. They pass because no test asserts that a browser can obtain a token it is required to send.

invariants: The token is returned only to a caller who already holds the session it belongs to.
Never logged, never in a URL, never in an unauthenticated response, never cacheable.
The gate's behaviour is unchanged: this movement makes the required token obtainable, it does not relax what is required.
One session's token is never valid for another.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Give the browser the CSRF token it is required to send. Every state-changing request in the product is refused today. The secret is minted at session creation and stored on the session row, the gate requires it on every state-changing method, and it is never returned to the client -- not in the login response, not in the session-status response, not as a cookie. So no write succeeds: no identity created, no credential stored, no device added, no backup requested. Reads work, so the product looks healthy while nothing can be saved.
output_contract: An operator can save something again: identities, credentials, devices and backup requests all reach the server.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One field on one response plus its cache headers, against a frozen contract that already says the client must present the token.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
The gradle command runs from ui2, the vitest command from ui2/frontend, the privacy gate from the repository root.
Every changed file names the clause it implements (C3, and the gate it must not change).
Run only the commands named above.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before every commit and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE states which headers you used to make the response uncacheable and what establishes the token is never logged.
risks: Returning the token to an unauthenticated caller, which would hand it to anyone who asks.
Leaving the response cacheable, which would let a shared cache serve one session's token to the next reader.
Adding a debug log line while working and leaving it in; the contract says never logged.
Relaxing the gate instead of supplying the token, which would remove the protection rather than complete it.

in: The authenticated session-status response carries the session's own CSRF token, under the key the client already reads. An unauthenticated caller's response is unchanged and carries nothing.

The response must not be cacheable by anything: set the headers that prevent a shared or browser cache from storing it, because a cached body would hand one session's token to whoever reads the cache next.

Tests: an authenticated status response carries a token that matches the session's stored secret; an unauthenticated one carries no such key at all; a state-changing request made with the token from that response is admitted, and one made without it is still refused exactly as today.
Remove the disclosed-limitation note from the frontend file header once it is no longer true, and say in the SESSION_CLOSE that it was removed.
out: Any change to the gate, its order, its status codes or its reason strings. GateChain is not edited by this movement.
Any change to the sessions schema, to how the secret is minted, or to its lifetime.
Any change to the origin check that follows the CSRF check.
Logging the token, anywhere, at any level. The contract says never logged and that includes a debug line added while working.
Putting the token in a URL, a query string, a redirect, or any response to an unauthenticated caller.
Any change to the frontend's request flow beyond deleting a note that has stopped being true.
